workflows.name: Fetch and split parcel scan assignments with HTTP Request in n8n

user.name: Anshul Namdev
user.bio: AI Automation Specialist | Technical Architect | Community Moderator

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This starter workflow for n8n Community Weekly Challenge 07 fetches your personal assignment and a set of parcel scan rows from an n8n-hosted HTTP endpoint, then splits the rows into individual scan items so you can build two calculations (parcel count and total work units).

How it works
Runs manually when you execute the workflow.
Sets your forum username and participant key for the run.
Sends an HTTP GET request to the n8n Community Weekly Challenge 07 data endpoint with your username as a query parameter and your participant key in the x-participant-key header.
Splits the returned rows array into individual scan items for downstream processing.
Leaves two disconnected placeholders where you add your own native logic to compute and output parcel_count (Question 1) and total_units (Question 2).

Setup
Check participation dates at https://marketing.app.n8n.cloud/webhook/cwc/challenge-07 and create or recover your participant account there. The permanent personal-data endpoint is available when C07 opens; importing this starter alone does not start your timer.
Enter your exact community username and current participant key in My settings. Run the shared fetch path when you are ready. The first personal data issue starts the clock, and later fetches retain the original assignment and start.
Build and test your own native calculations, then export a clean copy. Clear participantKey and remove passwords, credential references, saved run data and pinned data. Submit both integers, your JSON and your own explanation at https://marketing.app.n8n.cloud/webhook/cwc/challenge-07/submit.

Requirements
n8n with Manual Trigger, Edit Fields, HTTP Request and Split Out. The setup path was verified on n8n 2.35.5 and 2.43.7. A current CWC account is required when participation is open.

Customization
Use your returned personal selection rule and desk to build the missing native-node calculation. Both answer cards use the same 24 scans; no second HTTP request or supplied calculation is included.

Additional info
This is an intentionally unfinished starter for Community Weekly Challenge 07, The Exception Desk, and the Season 2 finale. No ranked solution or answer is supplied. AI assistance is not allowed for challenge entries. Code, Function and Function Item nodes are prohibited, including disabled or disconnected nodes. Explain your own approach in 40 to 2,000 characters and at least eight words. Correct eligible submissions are accepted automatically. Uploaded workflows remain private and are not executed by the challenge service. C07 is being prepared for launch; check the challenge website for participation dates.

workflows.name: Check manuscript references for retractions with Crossref, OpenAI and Gmail
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives a manuscript’s reference list via a header-authenticated webhook, checks each citation against Crossref (including Retraction Watch data) and doi.org, uses OpenAI to draft editor-facing integrity memos and author queries for flagged items, logs outcomes in n8n Data Tables, and re-checks accepted manuscripts weekly.

How it works
Receives a POST request with a manuscript ID, submitter email, and references list through a header-protected webhook.
Validates and normalizes the input, de-duplicates references, and reuses a recent closed result or returns an already-open case for the same manuscript when applicable.
Looks up each reference in the Crossref API (or runs a Crossref bibliographic search when no DOI is provided) and flags issues such as retractions, expressions of concern, corrections, DOI/citation mismatches, duplicates, or unresolved references.
For DOIs missing from Crossref, queries the doi.org handle API to distinguish non-Crossref registrations from non-existent (potentially fabricated) DOIs.
Aggregates all flags into an overall verdict floor and, when review is needed, uses an OpenAI agent (with Crossref and OpenAlex lookups) to produce a structured memo and draft author queries, then emails the report to the editor in Gmail.
Collects the editor’s decision via a form (optionally requiring integrity-officer approval to keep blocking references), writes the final outcome to n8n Data Tables, notifies the submitter by Gmail, and adds accepted/auto-cleared manuscripts to a watch list.
Runs every Monday to re-check watched DOIs in Crossref and reopens a new “post_publication_alert” check via webhook when a cited work’s status worsens.

Setup
Run the manual “Run once to set up” path to create the n8n Data Tables named reference_checks and reference_watch.
Create and attach an HTTP Header Auth credential for the intake webhook and for the “reopen check” HTTP request used by weekly monitoring.
Add OpenAI credentials (for the agent) and Gmail credentials (for editor notifications, submitter messages, integrity-officer approvals, and error alerts).
Replace placeholder values in “Reference check settings” and “Monitoring settings” (editor email, integrity officer email, Crossref mailto, ops email, and the workflow’s production webhook URL for reopening checks).

Requirements
A current n8n version with Data Tables and the AI Agent node (cloud or self-hosted).
An OpenAI API key, gpt-4.1-mini by default. The model is called only for lists with a medium or high flag.
A Gmail account. You can swap in Outlook, Slack or Teams for the notifications.
No other keys: Crossref, doi.org and OpenAlex are free public APIs. Crossref needs a real contact e-mail in crossref_mailto (polite pool); the workflow refuses to run with the placeholder. OpenAlex single-DOI lookups need no key.

Customization
Matching: title_match_threshold and mismatch_threshold in Reference check settings, plus STOP words in Read Crossref results.
Severities and actions: edit them in Read Crossref results and Read doi.org result. For example, make CORRECTED medium for clinical journals.
Reuse and open-check windows: REUSE_DAYS and OPEN_CHECK_DAYS in Check earlier checks and reuse window.
Follow-ups and blocking codes: MAX_FOLLOW_UPS and BLOCKING_CODES in Apply review policy. Timeouts are set in Wait for editor decision and Ask integrity officer to approve.
Weekly volume: MAX_DOIS in Collect DOIs to re-check.
Model: replace OpenAI with Anthropic, Gemini or a self-hosted model through Ollama.

Additional info
Limitations: Only works with a DOI, or with a citation that matches Crossref confidently, are checked; books, laws and web pages without a DOI usually end up UNRESOLVED for a person to verify. Retraction data is as complete as Crossref and Retraction Watch; a missing flag does not prove a cited work is sound. DOIs registered outside Crossref (DataCite, mEDRA) are reported as NOT_IN_CROSSREF and are not checked for retractions. METADATA_MISMATCH compares title words and year only, so it is medium, not high. Reference lists and citing context (no full text) are sent to the AI provider you connect. Decision support only: the editor decides.

workflows.name: Find decision makers and published emails from company pages with Apify and OpenAI
workflows.description:
Reads the team, about and leadership pages on the company domains you list through Apify and returns the named people with title, seniority, a confidence level and an email only when the company itself publishes one. Each person is scored by seniority and by how well the title matches the roles you sell to. It uses only the company's own public pages, no social networks or private data sources. Built for sales and partnership teams doing account research. Check local outreach and privacy rules before contacting anyone.

How it works
Daily schedule / manual run reads every setting from Config. A weekly schedule uses the same Config to send a report instead of running the actor.
Starts the Apify actor asynchronously, then waits and polls the run; FAILED, ABORTED, TIMED-OUT or too many polls stop with an error.
Downloads the dataset, validates rows and dedupes within the run and across runs (workflow static data, dedupeMemoryDays).
A transparent rule score runs first, then an LLM chain with a structured output parser reads each record against your plain-English aiCriteria and returns a fit score, verdict, summary, outreach angle and red flags. Calls are batched with a delay for rate limits, retried, and fall back to the rule score if the model fails.
Upserts every row to Google Sheets. Hot rows go to Slack as one approve / dismiss message (send-and-wait, 24 h limit) and the decision is written back to the sheet; warm rows go to an HTML email digest; cold rows stay in the sheet.
Weekly report: reads the sheet, summarises the last 7 days (tiers, approvals, top 10) and emails it.
A separate Error Trigger branch posts any failure to Slack.

Setup (about 15 minutes)
Create an HTTP Header Auth credential: name Authorization, value Bearer  (Apify Console > Settings > API & Integrations). Select it on the 3 Apify HTTP nodes.
Create a Google Sheet with a tab named in sheetTab and a header row matching the sheet columns (see Upsert to Google Sheets, plus status and reviewedAt). Paste its ID into googleSheetId.
Connect OpenAI (or swap the chat model sub-node for Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama...), Slack and Gmail; set slackChannelId and digestEmail in Config (also the channel on Slack: error alert).
In Config set actorInput.domains, minSeniority (manager, director, vp_partner, c_level) and targetTitles (fragments of the titles you sell to).
Write your ideal-lead description in aiCriteria; set aiWeight (0 = rules only, 1 = AI only).
Run once manually, check the sheet, then activate.

Customize
Edit weights in Score decision makers (seniority up to 35, title match 25, published email 20, confidence 15, source page 5).
Rows are keyed by domain and name, so the same person is not alerted twice.
Swap Gmail/Slack for Teams, Discord, HubSpot, Airtable, etc. Each delivery node only reads $json.

Disclosure: I maintain these Apify actors (account transparent_meteorite). The actor is a paid pay-per-event Apify tool; check its Store page for current pricing before scheduling.

workflows.name: Answer Japanese contact forms with OpenAI, Microsoft Teams and Gmail

user.name: Yuji
user.bio:
Marketing lead at a Japanese software company. I build practical n8n workflows for Japanese businesses, using AI to handle the Japanese language and business customs in everyday work.
日本の業務でそのまま使える、AIを組み込んだ n8n ワークフローを公開しています。

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow collects inquiries from an n8n form, matches them to FAQ entries stored in an n8n Data Table, drafts and keigo-checks a Japanese business email using OpenAI, posts it to Microsoft Teams for approval, and sends the approved reply via Gmail while logging the outcome.

How it works
Receives a new inquiry via an n8n form submission.
Loads all FAQ rows from the keigo_faq n8n Data Table, combines them, and adds your company name, signature, and the submitted contact details.
Uses OpenAI to classify the inquiry into a category and applies category-specific reply guidance, skipping messages classified as sales pitch or spam.
Selects up to three relevant FAQ entries by matching keyword hits in the message and compiles them into a single FAQ text block.
Uses OpenAI to generate a structured Japanese keigo email draft (subject, body, urgency, and staff check points) using only the matched FAQ content, then runs a second OpenAI pass to correct keigo issues and list the fixes.
Posts the checked draft, fixes, and FAQ topics to Microsoft Teams via an incoming webhook with a link to an approval form.
Waits for a reviewer to edit and approve the subject/body in the form, then sends the reply through Gmail if approved or skips sending if rejected.
Logs the decision (sent or skipped) with email, company, category, subject, and timestamp to the keigo_reply_log n8n Data Table.

Setup
Create two n8n Data Tables named keigo_faq (columns: topic, keywords, answer) and keigo_reply_log (columns: email, company, category, subject, status, logged_at).
Add an OpenAI credential for the Chat Model node (configured for gpt-5-mini).
Add a Gmail OAuth2 credential with permission to send mail from the account you want to reply from.
Create a Microsoft Teams Workflows (or compatible) incoming webhook and paste its URL into the Teams webhook HTTP request node.
Replace the default company_name and signature values with your own, and populate keigo_faq with your real FAQ topics, keywords, and answers (optionally run the sample FAQ loader once to seed example rows).

workflows.name: Create narrated Google Slides videos with Gemini TTS, Shotstack, Slack, and Drive
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Turns Google Slides speaker notes into a narrated video and re-voices only the slides that changed. A Gemini agent checks each slide against its notes and proposes pronunciations for a reading dictionary. Gemini TTS voices it, Slack approves it, and Shotstack renders captioned MP4s to Google Drive.

How it works
Starts from an n8n Form submission (with a Google Slides URL and options) or a weekday 8:00 schedule run.
Loads the Google Slides presentation, fingerprints each non-skipped slide (including speaker notes and voice settings), and compares it to previously stored slide records in an n8n Data Table to identify which slides changed.
For each changed slide, fetches a thumbnail, uses a Google Gemini agent to rewrite speaker notes into a narration script and flag issues, and looks up pronunciations in an n8n Data Table dictionary tool.
Generates WAV narration with Gemini TTS, uploads the slide image and audio to Shotstack ingest, waits for both sources to be ready, and upserts the slide’s script, captions, durations, and asset URLs back into the slides Data Table.
Builds a Slack review message summarizing what was re-voiced, any flagged issues, and proposed pronunciation readings, then waits for a reviewer to approve or reject.
If approved, builds a Shotstack edit timeline for all voiced slides (reusing unchanged assets), renders the MP4, uploads the finished video to Google Drive, logs the render to an n8n Data Table, and posts the Drive link to Slack.
If rejected, logs the rejection, clears fingerprints for the re-voiced slides so they are regenerated next run, and does not render a new video.

Setup
Add credentials for Google Slides and Google Drive (OAuth2), Slack (bot token with permission to post and use interactive messages), and Google Gemini/PaLM API (used for both the script agent and Gemini TTS).
Create a Shotstack API key and configure it as an HTTP Header Auth credential (x-api-key) on the Shotstack HTTP Request nodes, and set the Shotstack environment (stage or v1) in the workflow configuration.
Update the Workflow Configuration values for Slack channel ID, Google Drive folder ID, and a default Google Slides deck URL/ID, and adjust voice, language, captions, and rendering settings as needed.
Run the workflow once to create the required n8n Data Tables (narration_slides, narration_readings, narration_renders), then submit the form or enable the schedule trigger.

Requirements
Google Slides and Google Drive (OAuth2), Google Gemini API key, Shotstack API key (free sandbox works), Slack bot with chat:write, n8n with Data Tables

Customization
Change voice, speaking style, aspect ratio (9:16 for shorts), transition and captions in Workflow Configuration. Remove the Slack approval to publish automatically, or swap Google Drive for YouTube.

workflows.name: Qualify and triage leads with Google Gemini, HubSpot, Gmail, Slack and Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow captures website and Google Ads leads via webhooks, logs them to Google Sheets, and uses Google Gemini to qualify them against a Business Profile sheet, then creates HubSpot contacts and call tasks and sends Slack and Gmail alerts, reminders, and daily reports.

How it works
Receives new leads from a website form or Google Ads lead form via webhook, validates a shared secret key, normalizes the fields, and appends the lead to a Google Sheets Lead Log.
Loads services, service area, and qualification rules from a Google Sheets Business Profile and sends the lead details (or a matched Gmail reply) to Google Gemini to classify the lead and draft any needed email.
Updates the Lead Log with the AI outcome, priority, summary, and missing information details.
For qualified or not-a-fit leads, upserts the contact in HubSpot, creates an associated call task with a calculated due time, and emails the lead a confirmation.
For qualified leads, sends real-time alerts to a Slack channel and to the owner via Gmail.
For missing-info leads, emails the lead questions once and stores the Gmail thread ID so their reply can be matched and re-evaluated.
Runs hourly to check HubSpot task completion, send Slack/Gmail reminders for open qualified tasks, and escalate no-reply missing-info leads to “please call,” and runs daily at 6 PM to email a summary report from the Lead Log.

Setup
Create a Google Sheets Lead Log spreadsheet and a Business Profile spreadsheet with tabs and headers matching the notes for the Lead Log, Services, Service Area, and About and Rules.
Add credentials for Google Sheets, Gmail, Slack, and Google Gemini (Gemini API / Google AI), and create a HubSpot private app token with access to contacts and tasks.
Update the Config values for both sheet URLs, webhookSecret, businessName, alertEmail, slackChannel, timezone, and (optionally) hubspotOwnerId and reminder timing settings.
Copy the two webhook URLs and configure your website form and Google Ads Lead Form webhook to post leads with the secret key (header x-webhook-key or ?key= parameter).

workflows.name: Build monthly mileage reimbursement reports from Google Calendar with OpenAI and Dropbox

user.name: Gaetano Castaldo
user.bio:
Engineer and founder of Castaldo Solutions: we put AI and automation to work on the real processes of Italian small businesses, with a return you can measure within 90 days. Before that, fifteen years on enterprise projects, eleven in international consulting.

My templates are our own back office automations, made generic: e-invoices, mileage, month-end for the accountant, app monitoring, AI readiness. AI where it saves time, checks where a mistake costs money.

Less buzzwords, more results.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs monthly to turn Google Calendar trip events into a mileage reimbursement Excel, using OpenAI to parse free-text events and OpenStreetMap/OSRM to calculate driving distances, then uploads the file to Dropbox and (in live mode) prepares a Gmail draft for your accountant with validation checks.

How it works
Runs on the 1st of every month at 07:00 (or manually) and sets the month to process (previous month by default, or a manual override).
Pulls events for that month from Google Calendar and parses trips from titles like “Departure > Arrival, km, purpose”, while marking multi-day “Trasferta” events as away days.
Sends remaining in-month free-text events to OpenAI to extract whether they are car trips plus ordered stops, optional km, purpose, and one-way/round-trip.
For trips missing km (or when verification is enabled), geocodes unique stop names via OpenStreetMap Nominatim and calculates driving distance via the OSRM routing service.
Builds a per-day reimbursement table with totals, flags issues (km mismatch vs route, duplicate trips, excessive daily km, and AI-parsed trips to review), and generates an XLSX file.
Uploads the XLSX to Dropbox and, in live mode, records the month in an n8n Data Table to prevent duplicate drafting, creates a Gmail draft to the accountant with the Excel attached, and emails you an HTML summary.

Setup
Add credentials for Google Calendar OAuth2, OpenAI, Dropbox OAuth2, and Gmail OAuth2.
In the Settings node, set your Google Calendar ID, reimbursement rate per km, home base (usual departure), Dropbox folder path, recipient emails, and a valid OpenStreetMap-compliant User-Agent string.
If using live mode, ensure n8n Data Tables are available and set mode to "test" for a first run (optionally set monthOverride like "2026.10"), then switch mode to "live" and clear monthOverride before activating the schedule.

Requirements
Google Calendar, OpenAI, Dropbox and Gmail accounts, and an n8n version with data tables. No API key for OpenStreetMap: Nominatim and the public OSRM server are free within their usage policies.

Customization
Set readFreeTextWithAI to false to skip the AI; tune kmTolerancePercent and maxKmPerDay, or turn off checkDeclaredKm; set alwaysUseOpenStreetMap to true to ignore the km written in titles; change countryCodes for trips outside Italy.

Additional info
The AI never invents a departure: without one in the event or in homeBase, the event is listed instead of reimbursed. Labels, Excel columns and emails are in Italian on purpose, as an Italian accountant expects them; translate them in the Compose the reimbursement node. In Italy the rate per km comes from the ACI table for your car. To redo a month already drafted, delete its row in the Rimborsi km data table and run again.

user.name: Cheng Siong Chin
user.bio: Dr. Cheng Siong CHIN is an intelligent workflow creator specializing in AI-powered automation, multi-agent orchestration, and intelligent system integrations. He designs and builds end-to-end workflows that combine LLMs, APIs, and data pipelines to streamline complex processes and deliver production-ready automation solutions. Contact me to discuss custom AI workflows and agent architectures.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives ROV telemetry via webhook, derives safety and navigation metrics, then uses OpenAI multi-agent planning plus an independent safety validator to recommend or issue commands, notifying operators through Telegram, logging decisions in an n8n Data Table, and posting final commands to a topside control HTTP endpoint.

How it works
Receives ROV telemetry in a POST webhook request.
Validates required fields, derives metrics (distance to target, thruster margin, nearest sonar contact), and flags conditions and hard safety limit breaches.
If a hard limit is breached, generates an emergency safe command and immediately alerts the operator in Telegram.
Otherwise, loads recent mission decision history from an n8n Data Table and sends the telemetry plus history to an OpenAI supervisor agent that consults mission planning, navigation, perception, and safety specialist tools to produce a structured recommended command.
Runs an independent OpenAI safety validator to approve, modify, or veto the proposed command and packages the final decision with merged risk and alerts.
Posts a live status update to Telegram and routes the decision to either auto-execute, request operator approval via a Telegram form (with timeout defaulting to hold station), or issue a critical safe action with an alert.
Logs the final command to the n8n Data Table, sends it to the ROV topside control system via HTTP, and confirms the control system response in Telegram.

Setup
Add OpenAI API credentials for the supervisor, specialist, validator, liaison, and debrief agents.
Add Telegram bot credentials, replace all Telegram chat ID placeholders, and configure the bot to message the intended operator chat.
Create or select an n8n Data Table for the mission log (rov_mission_log) and set its ID in all Data Table nodes used for history and logging.
Set the ROV topside control system command endpoint URL in the HTTP Request node that sends commands to the vehicle.
Copy the webhook URL for the rov-telemetry endpoint into your telemetry source and send a test payload (including mission_id, depth_m, visibility_m, battery_or_power_pct, and tether_tension_kN) to verify the auto/approval/critical routes.

Customization
Swap models per agent, change authority rules in Decision Package, add Slack or email alerts, connect another vehicle API, adjust safety limits in the telemetry body, or change the debrief interval.

workflows.name: Check supplier invoices for fraud with PaperOffice AI and human review

user.name: PaperOffice AI
user.bio: PaperOffice AI is the European document platform for companies. These templates extract invoice data, redact or pseudonymize personal data, and answer questions from your own documents. Hosted in our own EU data center, GDPR-compliant, with no third-party AI subprocessors.

workflows.description:
Quick Overview
This workflow collects an invoice PDF via an n8n form, archives and extracts it in PaperOffice AI, cross-checks it against historical documents for IBAN changes, duplicates, and order/delivery mismatches, and then queues it for human review before tagging the document based on a signed PaperOffice webhook decision.

How it works
Receives an invoice PDF upload via an n8n form and validates required settings like the PaperOffice workspace ID and HITL agent UUID.
Uploads the PDF to PaperOffice AI, then runs PaperOffice AI invoice extraction to read key fields such as supplier, invoice number, total, IBAN, and line items.
Searches the PaperOffice AI workspace for earlier invoices by supplier, documents matching the order number, and documents with the same invoice number, and runs a PaperOffice AI duplicate check.
Reads OCR text from selected historical and order-related documents, extracts evidence (including validated IBANs), and optionally extracts structured data from the purchase order and delivery note.
Evaluates fraud and overbilling checks (extraction completeness, IBAN match/changed/unknown, possible duplicates, and ordered/delivered quantity mismatches) and writes a check report back onto the invoice document in PaperOffice AI.
Optionally starts a PaperOffice AI AI-DMS Ultra deep check, then enqueues the invoice into the PaperOffice AI HITL review queue and returns a JSON response indicating the task is queued.
Receives a signed PaperOffice AI review-decision webhook, verifies the HMAC signature, and tags the invoice in PaperOffice AI as either fraud-check:ready-for-payment or fraud-check:blocked.

Setup
Create an HTTP Bearer Auth credential with your PaperOffice AI user token (po_ut_…) and use it for all PaperOffice AI HTTP Request nodes.
Set your PaperOffice AI workspace ID and your HITL agent UUID in the Settings step.
Configure your PaperOffice AI HITL agent to call the production URL of the review-decision webhook and set the same signing secret in the HMAC signature configuration.
If you want optional deep checks, ensure your PaperOffice AI plan supports AI-DMS Ultra processing and keep the form option enabled for reviewers/requesters.

workflows.name: Book and manage form appointments with Google Calendar, OpenRouter, Gmail and Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow collects appointment requests via an n8n form, checks availability in Google Calendar, and either books the first matching slot or proposes alternatives. It uses OpenRouter to draft the email copy, sends emails through Gmail, logs each request to Google Sheets, and sends a reminder 24 hours before.

How it works
Receives an appointment request from an n8n Form with the customer’s details, preferred date, and preferred time window.
Calls the Google Calendar Free/Busy endpoint to fetch busy times for the selected calendar over the next two weeks.
Calculates the first available appointment slot within your opening hours and notice period, or generates up to three alternative openings if the preferred day is full.
Sends the booking status and times to OpenRouter to generate a JSON email subject and plain-text body.
If a slot is available, creates a Google Calendar event, emails the confirmation via Gmail, and appends a “booked” entry to Google Sheets.
If no slot is available on the requested day, emails the alternative times via Gmail and appends an “offered” entry to Google Sheets.
When a booking is more than 24 hours away, waits until 24 hours before the start time and sends a reminder email via Gmail.

Setup
Add credentials for Google Calendar OAuth2, Gmail OAuth2, and Google Sheets OAuth2.
Add an OpenRouter API key using HTTP Header Auth with header name Authorization and value Bearer YOUR_KEY.
Update the Booking Settings values (business name/description, timezone, calendar ID, opening days/hours, appointment duration, minimum notice, and optionally the booking form URL).
Create or select a Google Sheets spreadsheet with a Bookings sheet and headers Timestamp, Name, Email, Service, Slot, Status, then paste the spreadsheet document ID into both Google Sheets log steps.

Requirements
n8n (self-hosted or Cloud)
Google account with Calendar, Gmail and Sheets (OAuth2)
OpenRouter API key (the default free model costs $0)

Customization
Change appointment length, opening hours or open days in Booking Settings
Change the 30-minute slot step or the notice period in Find Free Slot
Swap the model in Write Email for any OpenRouter model
Set booking_form_url so the day-is-full email links back to the form

Additional info
Tested live against a real Google Calendar: two bookings for the same morning landed at 9:00 and 10:00 without double-booking; a morning blocked until 12 offered the same-day 12:00 PM slot first; a Saturday request offered the next weekday openings. The AI call retries up to 3 times because free models occasionally return a 502.

workflows.name: Screen and manage candidates with Gmail, Google Sheets, Google Drive and Nvidia Llama
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow ingests PDF resumes from Gmail (including Indeed application emails),extracts candidate details with an NVIDIA NIM LLM, stores the resume in Google Drive, and appends a deduplicated candidate record to Google Sheets, then sends acceptance or rejection emails and updates the sheet based on recruiter decisions and candidate replies.

How it works
Triggers every minute when a Gmail message arrives with a PDF attachment (or runs from a manual local-PDF test path) and normalizes the resume file plus sender and role metadata.
Extracts text from the PDF and sends it to the NVIDIA NIM chat completions API to parse structured candidate fields (name, email, phone, LinkedIn, portfolio, previous company, and position).
Uploads the original resume PDF to Google Drive and combines the Drive file link with the AI-parsed candidate data.
Checks the Google Sheets “Candidates” tab for existing emails to deduplicate, formats a candidate row (including a Drive hyperlink), and appends the new record to Google Sheets.
Triggers on a webhook or runs every minute to read Google Sheets decisions, filters rows marked Approve/Reject where no email has been sent, and routes them by decision.
Sends an acceptance questionnaire or a rejection email via Gmail and updates the corresponding Google Sheets row with the email status and processing timestamp.
Monitors Gmail for candidate replies to the questionnaire, uses the NVIDIA NIM API to extract questionnaire answers (CTC, notice period, location, etc.), and updates the matching Google Sheets row by candidate email.

Setup
Connect Gmail OAuth2 credentials for both reading incoming emails (resumes and replies) and sending acceptance/rejection emails.
Connect Google Sheets OAuth2 credentials, create a spreadsheet with a sheet named “Candidates”, and replace all instances of YOUR_SPREADSHEET_ID in the workflow (including the Sheets API call in the formatting step).
Connect Google Drive OAuth2 credentials and set YOUR_GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID in the Google Drive upload step.
Add your NVIDIA NIM API key by replacing the Bearer YOUR_API_KEY headers in both AI HTTP request steps.
If you use the webhook approval path, copy the production webhook URL for /candidate-approval and configure your approval source to POST the row data (including Email, Candidate ID, human_approval, and Email Status).

workflows.name: Find contractor leads in state license records with Apify, OpenAI, Sheets and Slack
workflows.description:
Reads public state contractor-license records (WA, TX, CT, CO, OR, DE) through Apify and scores each license for your offer. Set leadGoal to new to favour recently licensed contractors (suppliers, insurers, software, lenders) or renewal to favour licenses about to expire or just lapsed (renewal, compliance and insurance services). The key includes the expiry date, so a renewed license shows up again. Public records only; check each state's rules on contacting license holders.

How it works
Daily schedule / manual run reads every setting from Config. A weekly schedule uses the same Config to send a report instead of running the actor.
Starts the Apify actor asynchronously, then waits and polls the run; FAILED, ABORTED, TIMED-OUT or too many polls stop with an error.
Downloads the dataset, validates rows and dedupes within the run and across runs (workflow static data, dedupeMemoryDays).
A transparent rule score runs first, then an LLM chain with a structured output parser reads each record against your plain-English aiCriteria and returns a fit score, verdict, summary, outreach angle and red flags. Calls are batched with a delay for rate limits, retried, and fall back to the rule score if the model fails.
Upserts every row to Google Sheets. Hot rows go to Slack as one approve / dismiss message (send-and-wait, 24 h limit) and the decision is written back to the sheet; warm rows go to an HTML email digest; cold rows stay in the sheet.
Weekly report: reads the sheet, summarises the last 7 days (tiers, approvals, top 10) and emails it.
A separate Error Trigger branch posts any failure to Slack.

Setup (about 15 minutes)
Create an HTTP Header Auth credential: name Authorization, value Bearer  (Apify Console > Settings > API & Integrations). Select it on the 3 Apify HTTP nodes.
Create a Google Sheet with a tab named in sheetTab and a header row matching the sheet columns (see Upsert to Google Sheets, plus status and reviewedAt). Paste its ID into googleSheetId.
Connect OpenAI (or swap the chat model sub-node for Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama...), Slack and Gmail; set slackChannelId and digestEmail in Config (also the channel on Slack: error alert).
In Config choose leadGoal, targetTrades, newWithinDays and expiringWithinDays, and set actorInput.states and trade.
Write your ideal-lead description in aiCriteria; set aiWeight (0 = rules only, 1 = AI only).
Run once manually, check the sheet, then activate.

Customize
Edit weights in Score license leads (timing 40, phone 20, trade 15, contractor license 10, active 10, business 5).
Use mode: new_licenses with daysBack in actorInput for a feed of newly issued licenses only, or city / zip to narrow the area.
Swap Gmail/Slack for Teams, Discord, HubSpot, Airtable, etc. Each delivery node only reads $json.

Disclosure: I maintain these Apify actors (account transparent_meteorite). The actor is a paid pay-per-event Apify tool; check its Store page for current pricing before scheduling.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This webhook-driven workflow generates short-form video scripts and publishing copy with OpenAI, runs a local copy/duration audit, and renders approved 9:16 videos via Creatomate, returning either a creative kit, an audit checklist, a render job ID, or a final video URL.

How it works
Receives a POST webhook request (header-authenticated) with an action of draft, audit, render, or status.
Validates and sanitizes the request fields, enforcing limits and requiring explicit approval and rights confirmation before rendering.
For draft requests, sends a prompt to the OpenAI Chat Completions API to generate two hooks, a 4-scene storyboard, voiceover, hashtags, and SEO metadata, then returns a validated publishing kit for YouTube/TikTok/Instagram.
For audit requests, performs a deterministic local preflight to estimate duration and flag copy issues (for example length limits and exaggerated claims) and returns a checklist for human review.
For render requests, submits the approved Hook, Supporting_Text, and CTA into a specified Creatomate 1080×1920 template and returns the queued render job ID.
For status requests, fetches the Creatomate render job status and returns the final video URL and snapshot URL once the render succeeds (or errors if it fails).

Setup
Create a header-authenticated webhook credential for the incoming request and configure the calling app to send the required header.
Add an OpenAI API key as an HTTP Header Auth credential for the OpenAI request step.
Add a Creatomate API key as an HTTP Header Auth credential for the Creatomate render and status request steps.
In Creatomate, create a 1080×1920 template and ensure it contains elements named exactly Hook, Supporting_Text, and CTA, then use its template_id in render requests.
Build your client request payloads for each action (draft/audit/render/status) and only call render with approved=true and rights_confirmed=true after a manual review.

workflows.name: Audit Figma designs against your design system with Gemini and Slack
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Audits only changed Figma frames against your design system: contrast, font size, tap targets, unlinked tokens and detached components. A Gemini agent reviews each screenshot with your design guide. New issues become Figma comments, fixed ones get a ✅ reply, and Slack gets summaries and weekly reports.

How it works
Triggers when a Figma named version is saved via webhook, when someone submits the audit request form, or every Monday at 9:00.
Validates the request (including the Figma webhook passcode), loads the design guide from Google Docs, and fetches the Figma file structure.
Selects the target page, lists top-level frames, compares frame fingerprints against the stored snapshots in n8n Data Tables, and keeps only frames that changed (or forces a review for form requests).
For each changed frame, runs deterministic checks on the Figma node tree for contrast, font size, tap targets, token/style usage, and possible detached components, then loads any still-open findings for that frame.
Exports a PNG screenshot from Figma and sends it, the layer index, the design guide, and open issues to a Google Gemini agent that proposes new issues and marks previously reported AI issues as resolved when they appear fixed.
Reconciles new, still-open, and fixed findings by pinning new comments in Figma, replying in existing threads for fixed items, and updating the findings and frame snapshots in n8n Data Tables.
Posts an audit summary to a Slack channel after each run and posts a weekly design-health report to Slack based on the stored findings and frame metrics.

Setup
Create a Figma personal access token with access to read file content and write comments, and configure it as HTTP Header Auth for all Figma API requests (including the layer-inspection tool) and set a webhook passcode.
Add Google Docs OAuth credentials for reading your design guide and update the design guide document URL in the workflow configuration.
Add a Google Gemini API credential for the Gemini chat model used by the agent.
Add Slack credentials and set the target channel ID in the workflow configuration.
Update the workflow configuration values (page name, review focus, thresholds, limits, and timezone), and if using the Figma trigger, register a Figma FILE_VERSION_UPDATE webhook pointing to the production webhook URL with the same passcode.

Requirements
Figma account with a personal access token (file content read, comments write)
Google Gemini API key
Google account with the design guide in Google Docs
Slack workspace with a bot (chat:write) invited to the target channel
n8n with Data Tables (n8n Cloud or a recent self-hosted version)

Customization
Change contrast, font size and tap-target thresholds or the per-run limits in Workflow Configuration
Set reviewLanguage to get Figma comments in another language
Add your own rules in Run Design Checks; new rules are tracked and closed automatically like the built-in ones
Replace the Slack nodes with Gmail or Microsoft Teams, or move the weekly report to another day

Additional info
Tested end to end on a Figma file with color variables, text styles, a component and a detached copy. On the second run, fixed issues received a "✅ Fixed" reply and reaction in their original comment threads, and unchanged frames were skipped.

workflows.name: Chat with Thea, get a morning digest, and explore connections using OpenAI and Telegram
workflows.description:
Think of an Obsidian vault the whole world shares — except the reader is your AI. Your model stopped learning at its training cutoff, and web search hands it seven pages to guess from. Thea (thealibrary.org) is a library people fill and AIs read: dated news, new releases, real places, each entry written and checked by a person and kept with its source. This template shows three ways to read it, in three independent flows on one canvas.

How it works

1 · Chat with the library — Chat Trigger → AI Agent with three plain HTTP tools (no key): thea_search (one name), thea_find (browse by area, subject, country and date), thea_entry (the full entry by id, with its connections). Ask "Who is Karina from aespa?", "Hotels in 서귀포", "Any news from Japan since last week?", "Is this restaurant in Kuala Lumpur still open?". The agent answers only from what Thea returns and adds a source line.

2 · Morning world digest — Schedule (08:00) → your countries → thea_find?country=…&since=yesterday for each → flatten → one LLM call → Telegram. Thea dates every record by the event, so since returns what happened yesterday across the whole library: no scraping, no RSS, already deduplicated by people. Countries with nothing new get one honest line.

3 · Explore a name — an n8n Form takes one name → thea_search → thea_entry returns its connections with ids → one thea_entry per neighbour (who they are, their newest records) → the LLM writes a one-screen briefing: "aespa → SM Entertainment, four members, the fan meeting on 11-28". Walking the graph instead of searching names again.

Setup (2 minutes)

Open the three Chat Model nodes and attach one OpenAI credential — any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works (set Base URL to your local llama.cpp / Ollama / LM Studio; the key can be anything) or a real OpenAI key.
Flow 2: edit Your interests (countries, records per country, Telegram chat id) and attach a Telegram credential — or swap the last node for Slack / Email / Discord, the digest is plain text in {{ $json.text }}.
Flow 3: activate the workflow and open the form URL from the trigger node.

Thea needs no API key: 100 requests/hour per IP, data CC BY 4.0.

Notes

AI Agent pinned to v2.2 (v3.1 cannot call HTTP Request Tool nodes in n8n 2.44–2.45, issue #41604). Coverage is deepest in Korea today (1.07M places from public data) and grows wherever people add what they know — if something is missing, the agent says "not in Thea yet"; add it at thealibrary.org and every agent using this template sees it. Docs: thealibrary.org/docs · MCP server: org.thealibrary/thea.

user.name: Yuji
user.bio:
Marketing lead at a Japanese software company. I build practical n8n workflows for Japanese businesses, using AI to handle the Japanese language and business customs in everyday work.
日本の業務でそのまま使える、AIを組み込んだ n8n ワークフローを公開しています。

workflows.description:
Quick Overview
This workflow checks the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) weather warning feed every 30 minutes, compares changes per watched prefecture, posts alerts and an approval form to Microsoft Teams, and (after approval) emails affected customers via Gmail while tracking shipment and warning state in n8n Data Tables.

How it works
Runs every 30 minutes and loads workflow settings plus the saved warning state and open shipments from n8n Data Tables.
Downloads the public JMA XML warning feed, posts an error card to Microsoft Teams if the feed request fails, and otherwise parses the feed.
Filters feed entries to the watched prefectures, keeps the newest entry per prefecture, fetches each entry’s detail XML, and extracts the active warning types and headline.
Compares the current warnings to the previously saved warnings per prefecture, routes only newly issued/changed warnings and all-clear events, and upserts the latest state back to the warning state table.
For newly issued warnings, matches the affected prefecture (and the warehouse prefecture) against pending shipments due within the lookahead window in the open shipments table.
Uses OpenAI to draft a Japanese internal alert plus a polite customer email template with placeholders, then posts the alert to Microsoft Teams and, if shipments are affected, posts a Teams card with a “Review and send” link to an n8n approval form.
Waits for staff to approve or skip sending (with a reminder and expiry if no response), then sends one Gmail email per affected order and updates each order record with the send result and posts a send summary to Microsoft Teams.

Setup
Create two n8n Data Tables named weather_alert_state (prefecture, warnings, reported_at) and open_shipments (order_id, customer_name, email, ship_to_prefecture, ship_date, status, notice_sent, notified_at) and populate open_shipments with your pending orders.
Add an OpenAI credential (Chat model) and a Gmail OAuth2 credential for the mailbox that sends customer notices.
Configure a Microsoft Teams Workflows/Incoming Webhook URL and paste it into the teams_webhook_url setting, then update watched prefectures, warehouse prefecture, lookahead days, reminder timing, and company signature in the settings node.

workflows.name: Detect funding, layoff, lawsuit, and M&A news for watched companies with Apify, OpenAI, Gmail, Google Sheets, and Slack
workflows.description:
Watches publisher RSS feeds (and the public GDELT news index when reachable) for the companies and keywords you list, tags business events and headline sentiment, and scores each new article by event type, tone, how many outlets repeat it and how fresh it is. Built for sales trigger-event hunting, PR and comms monitoring, and analysts.

How it works
Daily schedule / manual run reads every setting from Config. A weekly schedule uses the same Config to send a report instead of running the actor.
Starts the Apify actor asynchronously, then waits and polls the run; FAILED, ABORTED, TIMED-OUT or too many polls stop with an error.
Downloads the dataset, validates rows and dedupes within the run and across runs (workflow static data, dedupeMemoryDays).
A transparent rule score runs first, then an LLM chain with a structured output parser reads each record against your plain-English aiCriteria and returns a fit score, verdict, summary, outreach angle and red flags. Calls are batched with a delay for rate limits, retried, and fall back to the rule score if the model fails.
Upserts every row to Google Sheets. Hot rows go to Slack as one approve / dismiss message (send-and-wait, 24 h limit) and the decision is written back to the sheet; warm rows go to an HTML email digest; cold rows stay in the sheet.
Weekly report: reads the sheet, summarises the last 7 days (tiers, approvals, top 10) and emails it.
A separate Error Trigger branch posts any failure to Slack.

Setup (about 15 minutes)
Create an HTTP Header Auth credential: name Authorization, value Bearer  (Apify Console > Settings > API & Integrations). Select it on the 3 Apify HTTP nodes.
Create a Google Sheet with a tab named in sheetTab and a header row matching the sheet columns (see Upsert to Google Sheets, plus status and reviewedAt). Paste its ID into googleSheetId.
Connect OpenAI (or swap the chat model sub-node for Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama...), Slack and Gmail; set slackChannelId and digestEmail in Config (also the channel on Slack: error alert).
In Config set actorInput.companies and keywords, timespan (match it to the schedule), priorityEvents (events that should go to Slack), watchSentiment and majorPublishers. Use excludeWords to drop noise such as coupons and sponsored posts.
Write your ideal-lead description in aiCriteria; set aiWeight (0 = rules only, 1 = AI only).
Run once manually, check the sheet, then activate.

Customize
Edit weights in Score news significance (priority event 40, tone 15, other outlets 15, major publisher 10, keyword match 10, freshness 10).
Add eventFilter to actorInput to have the actor return only funding, layoffs, lawsuit, hiring or acquisition stories.
Add your own rssFeeds for niche trade press.
Swap Gmail/Slack for Teams, Discord, HubSpot, Airtable, etc. Each delivery node only reads $json.

Disclosure: I maintain these Apify actors (account transparent_meteorite). The actor is a paid pay-per-event Apify tool; check its Store page for current pricing before scheduling.

How it works

Normalizes incoming form fields into a consistent lead object (name, email, phone, company, message, source) and prepares an OpenAI Chat Completions request.
Sends the lead details to the OpenAI API to generate a 1–10 score plus a short reason and summary in JSON.
Parses the OpenAI response and attaches the score, reason, and summary to the lead record.
Sends a thank-you email to the lead using your SMTP mail server with a booking link for follow-up.
Upserts the lead as a contact in HubSpot using the email address as the unique identifier.
Posts a message to Slack via an incoming webhook when the lead score is greater than or equal to the configured hot-lead score.

Setup
Configure the webhook URL in your form tool to POST lead submissions to the workflow’s “New lead” production webhook endpoint.
Add an HTTP Header Auth credential for OpenAI (Authorization: Bearer ) and attach it to the OpenAI request.
Add an HTTP Header Auth credential for HubSpot (Authorization: Bearer ) and attach it to the HubSpot upsert request.
Add an SMTP credential for sending email and set the from address, business name, booking link, Slack incoming webhook URL, and hot-lead score in the Config values.
